lines: This dam should still be cooling down today.
This dam should STILL be cooling down TODAY.
Hoover Dam. Seven hundred twenty six feet of concrete, wedged into Black Canyon on the Colorado River.
Hoover Dam. 726 FEET of concrete, wedged into Black Canyon on the Colorado River.
To build it, engineers had to beat two impossible problems. And the second one is wild.
To build it, engineers had to beat TWO impossible problems. And the second one is WILD.
Problem one: a whole river was in the way. So they blasted four tunnels through solid rock, each fifty six feet wide, and sent the Colorado around the site.
Problem ONE: a whole RIVER was in the way. So they blasted FOUR tunnels through solid rock, each 56 FEET wide, and sent the Colorado AROUND the site.
Problem two: heat. Concrete gets hot as it sets. Pour this wall in one go, and it would take a hundred and twenty five years to cool, and crack as it shrank.
Problem TWO: HEAT. Concrete gets hot as it sets. Pour this wall in one go, and it would take 125 YEARS to cool, and CRACK as it shrank.
So they didn't pour one dam. They poured about two hundred and fifteen giant blocks, up to sixty feet wide, five feet at a time.
So they didn't pour ONE dam. They poured about 215 giant BLOCKS, up to 60 FEET wide, 5 FEET at a time.
And here's the genius part. Inside every block they buried steel pipes, and pumped river water, then chilled water from a refrigeration plant, through them to pull the heat out.
And here's the GENIUS part. Inside every block they buried steel PIPES, and pumped river water, then CHILLED water from a refrigeration plant, through them to pull the heat out.
Then they filled the pipes and every gap with grout, locking the blocks into one solid wall.
Then they filled the pipes and every gap with GROUT, locking the blocks into ONE solid wall.
Those pipes are still in there. Hundreds of miles of them. And there's enough concrete here to pave a road from San Francisco to New York.
Those pipes are STILL in there. HUNDREDS of miles of them. And there's enough concrete here to pave a road from SAN FRANCISCO to NEW YORK.
So it isn't one piece. And that's exactly why it isn't still cooling today.
So it ISN'T one piece. And that's exactly why it isn't STILL cooling today.
Follow for a new wonder every day.
FOLLOW for a new wonder every day.
